  • Colposcopy: Advanced evaluation, colposcopic biopsy, and safe surveillance following HPV positivity and abnormal cervical smear results, avoiding unnecessary interventions.
  • Advanced surgery in recurrent gynecologic cancers: Experienced surgical management of recurrent gynecologic tumors, including heated intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) and pressurized intraperitoneal aerosol chemotherapy (PIPAC) in ovarian cancer.
  • Fertility-preserving gynecologic oncology: Modern and safe approaches aimed at preserving fertility in appropriately selected patients during cancer treatment.
  • Preventive gynecology and early diagnosis: Risk assessment, screening programs, and individualized prevention strategies for gynecologic cancers.
  • Minimally invasive surgical techniques: Laparoscopic and robotic surgery focused on less postoperative pain, faster recovery, and early return to daily life.

  • Urogynecologic procedures: Surgical and non-surgical management of genital prolapse (uterine prolapse) and urinary incontinence.
  • Menopause management: Evidence-based evaluation of menopausal symptoms with individualized treatment and follow-up to improve quality of life.

Yeditepe University Koşuyolu Hospital in Kadıköy, on the Asian side of Istanbul, has 180 beds, six intensive care beds and nine operating theatres on 35,000 m² of indoor space. Around 100 specialists and academic physicians work at the hospital.

About the hospital

The hospital focuses on neurosciences and oncology: neurosurgery, cancer surgery, medical oncology, bone marrow transplantation for children and adults, orthopaedics, thoracic surgery, ENT, general surgery, gastroenterology, nuclear medicine and interventional radiology.

An intraoperative 3 Tesla MRI scanner is installed in the neurosurgical operating theatre. As part of infection prevention, the surfaces of the hospital were treated with a boron-based antimicrobial coating developed at Yeditepe University.

Koşuyolu Hospital holds the JCI accreditation as an Academic Medical Center (valid until 2028).

Yeditepe University Kozyatağı Hospital in Ataşehir, on the Asian side of Istanbul, opened on 26 August 2005. It has 190 beds and a wide range of departments, from internal medicine and cardiology to obstetrics, IVF and paediatrics.

The building was planned with fire-resistant, scratch-resistant and antibacterial materials. Particular attention is paid to hygiene and sterilisation: in addition to manual disinfection, all patient beds can be cleaned with a high-temperature water spray system.

A thigh lift removes excess skin and fat from the inner or outer thighs and tightens the tissue underneath – often after major weight loss or with age – for smoother, firmer contours. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.

General anaesthesia

Hospital stay

Within hours

Compression garment

In the first weeks

Stay in Türkiye

General information; your surgeon plans the details for you personally.

Who it may be suitable for

  • You have loose skin and excess fat on your thighs, for example after major weight loss or with age.
  • Your weight has been stable for some time.
  • You are in good general health.

Whether the procedure is suitable for you is decided by the surgeon after a personal assessment.

Options

Inner thigh lift

Incisions along the inner thighs for loose skin on the inside of the legs.

Outer thigh lift

Incisions along the outer thighs to tighten the outer contour.

How the operation is performed

Consultation before surgery

The surgeon assesses the areas of concern, discusses your wishes and makes a personal surgical plan.

Anaesthesia and preparation

You receive general anaesthesia. The area is marked to guide the incisions.

Removing excess skin and fat

Incisions are made along the inner or outer thighs; excess skin and fat are removed and the tissue underneath is tightened.

Closure and recovery

The incisions are closed with sutures and compression garments are put on. You usually stay in hospital for 1–2 nights.

The veneers are made in a dental laboratory to match the shape, colour and size you planned.

After a trial fitting, the veneers are bonded and fine-tuned for comfort and a natural look.

All-on-4 and All-on-6 replace a complete row of teeth in the upper or lower jaw with a fixed bridge on four or six titanium implants – a fixed alternative to removable dentures. With six implants, the biting forces are spread more evenly. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the dentist in Istanbul and organises your stay.

Quick facts

Anaesthesia

Local anaesthesia or sedation

Trips to Türkiye

Usually 2

1st visit

About 3–5 days

Healing time

3–6 months

2nd visit

About 5–7 days

General information; your dentist plans the details for you personally.

Who it may be suitable for

  • You are missing most or all of your teeth in one or both jaws, or your teeth are badly damaged.
  • You wear dentures and would like a fixed solution.
  • You are in good general health; if there is little jawbone, bone grafting can be considered.

Whether the treatment is suitable for you is decided by the dentist after a personal assessment.

Options

All-on-4

A full arch on four angled implants – makes the most of the available bone and often avoids bone grafting.

All-on-6

A full arch on six implants – more stability and an even distribution of the biting forces.

How the treatment works

Preparation and anaesthesia

Breast reduction reduces the size and weight of very large breasts. It can relieve back and neck pain, restricted movement and skin irritation and creates a more balanced silhouette. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.

General anaesthesia

Stay in Türkiye

General information; your surgeon plans the details for you personally.

Who it may be suitable for

  • Large breasts cause you physical discomfort, for example back, neck or shoulder pain.
  • You suffer from skin irritation, a poor posture or have difficulty finding clothes that fit.
  • You would like breasts in better proportion to your body.
  • Your weight has been stable for some time.
  • You are in good general health.

Whether the procedure is suitable for you is decided by the surgeon after a personal assessment.

How the operation is performed

Preparation and anaesthesia

After a detailed consultation about your complaints, wishes and health, the operation takes place under general anaesthesia.

Incision and tissue removal

Incisions are made around the areola, vertically down the breast and sometimes along the breast crease. Excess breast tissue, fat and skin are removed.

Reshaping and nipple position

The remaining tissue is shaped and, in most cases, the nipple and areola are moved higher while keeping their connection to nerves and blood supply.

Closure and recovery

The incisions are closed with fine sutures and a supportive bra is put on. You usually stay in hospital for one night.

Stay in Türkiye

Planned individually with the clinic

General information; your surgeon plans the details for you personally.

Who it may be suitable for

  • You have local fat deposits that do not respond to diet and exercise.
  • Your weight is stable and close to your goal weight.
  • You are in good general health.
  • You understand that liposuction shapes the body but is not a weight-loss treatment.

Whether the procedure is suitable for you is decided by the surgeon after a personal assessment.

Common treatment areas

Abdomen and waist

Including the flanks for a smoother waistline.

Thighs

Inner and outer thighs.

Arms, back and chest

Upper arms, the back and – for men – the chest.

Neck and chin

For a more defined jawline.

How the operation is performed

Consultation before surgery

The surgeon assesses the areas to be treated, discusses your wishes and makes a personal treatment plan.

Anaesthesia and preparation

Depending on the area and extent, you receive local anaesthesia with sedation or general anaesthesia. The areas are marked and prepared.

Fat removal and contouring

Through small incisions, a thin cannula loosens and removes the fat – depending on the plan also with Vaser or laser-assisted techniques – and the area is shaped evenly.

Closure and recovery

The small incisions are closed and a compression garment is put on. Depending on the extent, you go home the same day or after one night.

Medical microbiology provides the laboratory testing behind the diagnosis and treatment of infections. The laboratories at our partner hospital support inpatient, outpatient and emergency care across bacteriology, virology, parasitology, mycology, molecular microbiology and infection immunology, with a broad and regularly updated test panel. MedLuxLife coordinates sample collection during your visit and ensures your results are translated and shared with your doctors.

Treatments and services

Bacteriology

Identification of bacteria and antibiotic susceptibility testing, combining classical culture with rapid confirmatory methods and same-day stained microscopy.

Mycobacteriology (tuberculosis)

Isolation and identification of acid-fast organisms such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Mycobacterium avium complex, including molecular methods and the Quantiferon TB Gold test.

Virology

Antigen and antibody serology, sensitive detection of HIV and hepatitis agents, and confirmatory testing where needed.

Parasitology

Diagnosis of parasitic infections using classical methods supported by serological tests.

Mycology

Identification of yeasts, dermatophytes and moulds, plus galactomannan antigen testing for suspected aspergillus infection in immunocompromised patients.

Molecular microbiology

PCR-based detection, genotyping and viral load testing, including viruses monitored after transplantation.

Syndromic molecular panels

Rapid multiplex testing of blood cultures, respiratory, gastrointestinal, cerebrospinal and joint fluid samples, with simultaneous detection of resistance genes.

Infection immunology

Immunological tests that support the diagnosis of infectious diseases.

Round-the-clock service

The laboratory operates 24 hours a day and works closely with clinicians on diagnosis and treatment.

Selected tests

  • Bacterial culture and antibiotic susceptibility testing
  • Stained microscopy of clinical samples
  • Acid-fast bacteria staining
  • Quantiferon TB Gold
  • Galactomannan antigen test
  • Hepatitis B virus DNA
  • Hepatitis C virus RNA
  • Varicella zoster virus (VZV)
  • Epstein-Barr virus (EBV DNA)
  • Cytomegalovirus (CMV DNA)
  • Polyomavirus (BK/JC virus)
  • Human papillomavirus (HPV DNA) and genotyping
  • Viral load tests
  • MRSA (real-time PCR)
  • VRE (real-time PCR)
  • Neisseria gonorrhoeae (real-time PCR)
  • Chlamydia (real-time PCR)
  • Syndromic panels for blood culture, respiratory, gastrointestinal, CSF and joint fluid samples
  • Resistance gene detection

Medical genetics diagnoses inherited and non-inherited conditions caused by changes in genes, and helps individuals and families understand their risks, including carrier status and risks for future children. The genetic diagnosis centre at our partner hospital offers genetic consultations and counselling alongside cytogenetic, molecular cytogenetic and molecular genetic testing in ISO 15189 accredited laboratories. MedLuxLife coordinates your appointments and the practical steps of your visit.

Treatments and services

Genetic consultation

Outpatient examination by a medical geneticist to assess whether a genetic condition may be present.

Genetic counselling

Explanation of results, risk assessment for relatives and future generations, and planning of preventive options, also for families referred from other centres.

Prenatal genetic diagnosis

Testing during pregnancy when screening suggests increased risk, with advanced maternal age, or when a parent carries a known genetic condition.

Postnatal genetic diagnosis

Testing in children and adults when a genetic cause is suspected, including recurrent miscarriage, infertility and hereditary neurological or muscle diseases.

Cytogenetics

Karyotype analysis on blood, amniotic fluid, chorionic villus, fetal blood and bone marrow samples.

Molecular cytogenetics

FISH testing, including rapid detection of common chromosomal changes and microdeletion syndromes, and molecular karyotyping (array CGH).

Molecular genetic testing

DNA analyses for single-gene diseases and carrier status.

Oncology and haematology genetics

FISH and DNA analyses on tumour tissue and bone marrow, used as markers for disease course and possible response to chemotherapy.

Interdisciplinary cooperation

Close collaboration with paediatrics, obstetrics and gynaecology, internal medicine, neurology, neurosurgery and pathology.

Situations in which genetic testing may be considered

  • Increased risk of a chromosomal anomaly in pregnancy screening
  • Advanced maternal age
  • Known carrier status for a chromosomal or single-gene disease
  • Down syndrome (trisomy 21) and other common chromosomal anomalies - rapid FISH on amniocentesis samples
  • Rapid chromosomal analysis on chorionic villus biopsy samples
  • Karyotype and DNA analyses on fetal blood samples
  • Congenital anomalies
  • Growth, developmental and intellectual disabilities
  • Short stature
  • Global developmental delay
  • Recurrent miscarriage
  • Infertility
  • Single-gene diseases more common in consanguineous families
  • Hereditary neurological and muscle diseases appearing in adulthood
  • Suspected inherited predisposition to thrombosis
  • Oncology and haematology patients (tumour tissue and bone marrow analyses)

Ultrasonography including Doppler, 3D and 4D imaging.

Real-time X-ray imaging used for dynamic studies and to guide procedures.

MedLuxLife coordinates assessments, treatment schedules and family logistics at our partner hospital.

Treatments and services

Blood disorders

Diagnosis and treatment of anaemias, blood production disorders and bone marrow failure.

Childhood cancers

Care for leukaemia and other tumours in children, planned with child-specific approaches.

Hereditary conditions

Follow-up of inherited blood and immune system disorders such as thalassaemia and sickle cell disease.

Bone marrow transplantation link

Outpatient and inpatient treatment in cooperation with the paediatric bone marrow transplantation clinic when needed.

Conditions treated

  • Leukaemia
  • Blood production disorders
  • Thalassaemia (Mediterranean anaemia)
  • Sickle cell disease
  • Bone marrow failure
  • Genetic diseases
  • Immune system diseases
  • Tumours

Paediatric oncology focuses on the diagnosis, treatment and long-term follow-up of cancers in children and adolescents up to the age of 18, including solid tumours, lymphomas and leukaemias. Childhood cancers behave differently from adult cancers and call for care designed around young patients and their families. MedLuxLife coordinates assessments and treatment at our partner hospital, helping families with records, appointments, travel and communication throughout the course of care.

Treatments and services

Diagnosis and staging

Thorough evaluation of suspected childhood tumours, lymphomas and leukaemias to establish the diagnosis and the extent of the disease.

Surgery

Surgical removal of tumours may form part of the treatment plan, depending on tumour type and spread.

Chemotherapy

Drug-based cancer treatment planned individually for each child, delivered on an inpatient or outpatient basis.

Radiotherapy

Radiation treatment may be recommended for certain tumour types as part of a combined plan.

Immunotherapy

Treatments that engage the immune system can be considered for selected childhood cancers.

Stem cell transplantation

Stem cell transplantation is among the treatment options for some childhood cancers and blood diseases.

Paediatric haematology-oncology clinic

Outpatient and inpatient care in a dedicated paediatric haematology-oncology clinic, with single rooms that allow a parent to stay with the child during monitoring and treatment.

Outpatient chemotherapy unit

A day unit for short treatments and blood transfusions, so that many children can return home the same day.

Dedicated children's outpatient floor

Outpatient consultations take place on a separate floor reserved for children with cancer, leukaemia and blood diseases.

Long-term follow-up

Structured follow-up after treatment to monitor recovery and the child's ongoing health.

Childhood tumours evaluated

  • Brain tumours
  • Wilms' tumour and other kidney tumours
  • Neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroblastoma (adrenal tumours)
  • Soft tissue sarcomas (muscle and connective tissue tumours)
  • Bone tumours
  • Retinoblastoma (eye tumour)
  • Germ cell tumours
  • Hepatoblastoma and hepatocellular carcinoma (liver tumours)
  • Lymphomas
  • Leukaemias
  • Other rare childhood tumours

  • Recent laboratory results

  • Pathology and biopsy reports
  • Previous imaging (MRI, CT or PET-CT) on CD/DVD with reports

Paediatric cardiology looks after the heart and circulation of children from birth through adolescence. Specialists assess congenital and acquired heart conditions and plan treatment together with paediatric heart surgeons and other specialties. MedLuxLife arranges examinations and follow-up at our partner hospital and supports families during every visit.

Treatments and services

Specialist examination

Every assessment starts with a thorough examination by a paediatric cardiologist.

Echocardiography and ECG

Heart ultrasound, electrocardiogram and other tests help establish the diagnosis.

Follow-up of prenatal findings

Heart findings detected before birth by obstetricians are evaluated by paediatric cardiologists after delivery.

Individual treatment plans

A treatment plan is prepared for each child, with regular monitoring of how treatment is progressing.

Lifelong follow-up

Some children need regular cardiac check-ups over many years, so close contact with the care team is maintained.

Interdisciplinary care

Collaboration with paediatric cardiac surgery, paediatric haematology and oncology, genetics and other paediatric specialties.

Paediatric surgery deals with conditions requiring surgical care in infants, children and adolescents, from the prenatal period up to the age of 18. Treatment is tailored to the child's age and development, with open, endoscopic and laparoscopic techniques available. MedLuxLife coordinates consultations, surgery dates and aftercare at our partner hospital, so that families can focus on their child.

Treatments and services

Prenatal consultation

Surgical evaluation can begin before birth when a condition requiring surgery is identified during pregnancy.

Digestive system surgery

Diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of surgical conditions affecting the digestive tract in children.

Urinary tract surgery

Surgical care for conditions of the kidneys, bladder and urinary tract in childhood.

Chest surgery (non-cardiac)

Treatment of surgical conditions within the chest cavity, excluding the heart.

Open, endoscopic and laparoscopic techniques

Alongside conventional surgery, endoscopic and laparoscopic methods are used where suitable.

Day surgery

Many procedures allow same-day discharge, including inguinal hernia repair, hydrocele repair, treatment of undescended testicles, circumcision, catheter placement and endoscopic procedures.

Pain management

Specific pain-relief measures aim to keep children comfortable in hospital and after returning home.

Paediatric urology

Coordinated care

The paediatrics department provides diagnosis and treatment for children from birth to 18 years of age, with outpatient clinics, an inpatient ward and intensive care areas designed for children. It is organised into a newborn section (0-28 days) and a child section (0-18 years), with subspecialties working together as a multidisciplinary team. MedLuxLife helps families access the right paediatric specialist at our partner hospital and coordinates appointments, travel and communication.

Treatments and services

General paediatric care

Outpatient, inpatient and intensive care services for children aged 0-18 in child-friendly settings.

Newborn care

The neonatal section serves babies up to 28 days old through a neonatal unit, a neonatal observation unit and a neonatal intensive care unit.

Breastfeeding support

The hospital follows the UNICEF and WHO Baby-Friendly approach, with specially trained staff helping mothers establish and maintain breastfeeding.

Paediatric allergy

Testing and treatment for allergic diseases, including skin tests, blood allergy tests, lung function tests, allergen provocation tests, food tests, anaesthetic drug tests and allergy vaccination (immunotherapy).

Paediatric endocrinology

Assessment of hormonal and metabolic problems such as growth disorders, diabetes, thyroid and puberty-related conditions.

Paediatric haematology-oncology

Diagnosis and treatment of blood diseases and childhood cancers, with outpatient and inpatient care in a paediatric bone marrow transplantation clinic.

Paediatric gastroenterology, hepatology and nutrition

Care for diseases of the oesophagus, stomach, duodenum, small and large intestine, liver and gallbladder, as well as nutritional disorders.

Paediatric surgery

Treatment of urological, genital, digestive and respiratory conditions and newborn anomalies, including non-cardiac thoracic, oncological, digestive and endocrine surgery, paediatric gynaecology, trauma surgery, diagnostic and interventional endoscopy, and laparoscopic and thoracoscopic procedures.

Paediatric nephrology

Diagnosis and treatment of congenital and acquired problems of the kidneys, urinary tract, bladder and urethra.

Paediatric rheumatology

Outpatient care for childhood rheumatic diseases affecting joints, muscles, blood vessels and skin.

  • Childhood tumours
  • Diseases of the oesophagus, stomach and intestines
  • Liver and gallbladder diseases
  • Nutritional disorders
  • Kidney and urinary tract disorders
  • Childhood rheumatic diseases

Balanced nutrition plays an important part in both preventing illness and supporting medical treatment. The nutrition and dietetics team at our partner hospital assesses your eating habits and body composition and develops a personalised nutrition plan with regular follow-up. MedLuxLife coordinates your consultations and can combine them with other treatments during your stay.

Treatments and services

Initial assessment and body analysis

Review of eating habits plus body analysis to measure fat, muscle and water percentages and regional fat distribution.

Personalised nutrition therapy

A plan based on age, height, sex, physical activity and blood test results, with regular follow-up appointments.

Inpatient nutrition

Menus for hospitalised patients are planned together with doctors, the patient and relatives, and monitored from preparation to delivery.

Home nutrition education

Guidance during the hospital stay on how to continue the nutrition plan at home.

Support around obesity surgery

Nutritional preparation before bariatric surgery to help reduce surgical risk, and guidance on sustainable lifestyle changes afterwards.

Home-based monitoring

On request, follow-up at home for elderly or bedridden patients.

Corporate services

Nutrition and diet counselling and customised menu planning for private organisations.

Education and awareness

Seminars, training sessions and media work to raise awareness of healthy eating.

Areas of medical nutrition

  • Medical nutrition in obesity
  • Medical nutrition in diabetes mellitus
  • Medical nutrition in liver diseases
  • Medical nutrition in kidney diseases
  • Medical nutrition in high blood pressure and cardiovascular diseases
  • Medical nutrition for rheumatism and gout
  • Medical nutrition for oncology patients
  • Malnutrition (extreme thinness and inadequate nutrition)
  • Nutrition with food allergies and food intolerances
  • Healthy nutrition in infancy, childhood and adolescence
  • Healthy nutrition during pregnancy and breastfeeding
  • Sports nutrition

Lifestyle counselling

Vaccination and prevention

Vaccines and preventive measures recommended for people who are prone to immune system disorders, to help lower the risk of infection.

Nephrology is the branch of internal medicine concerned with kidney health and disease, including blood pressure, fluid and electrolyte balance, and the effects of other illnesses and medicines on the kidneys. At our partner hospital, nephrologists provide outpatient, inpatient and intensive care services, all forms of dialysis and assessment for kidney transplantation with lifelong follow-up. MedLuxLife coordinates your appointments and treatment schedule and organises the practical details of your stay.

Treatments and services

Outpatient clinic

Diagnosis and treatment of kidney diseases, preventive care for people at higher risk such as those with diabetes or hypertension, and supportive care for advanced kidney disease.

Inpatient care and consultations

Ward-based care and follow-up, plus nephrology consultations for other departments.

Kidney effects of other conditions and medicines

Evaluation of how diabetes, hypertension, rheumatological disease, acute illness or long-term medicines such as chemotherapy, anti-rheumatic drugs and cortisone may affect the kidneys.

Intensive care kidney support

Haemodialysis, haemofiltration, haemodiafiltration and continuous venovenous haemofiltration for patients with acute kidney failure.

Haemoperfusion and plasmapheresis

Blood purification treatments that may be used when clinically indicated.

Haemodialysis

Acute or chronic haemodialysis, with session frequency and length adjusted to remaining kidney function and diet.

Peritoneal dialysis

Peritoneal dialysis including continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD), which patients perform themselves at home.

Kidney transplantation

Assessment for transplantation in end-stage kidney disease, with transplantation through the organ transplant unit and lifelong post-transplant follow-up.

Conditions treated

  • Structural and functional disorders of the urinary system
  • Hereditary kidney diseases
  • Polycystic kidney disease
  • Familial Mediterranean fever
  • Amyloidosis
  • Kidney stone disease
  • Fluid, electrolyte and acid-base disorders
  • Hypertension and hypertensive kidney disease
  • Kidney and urinary tract infections
  • Diabetes-related kidney disease
  • Kidney involvement in rheumatological diseases
  • Kidney problems related to fluid loss, heart failure or sepsis
  • Medication-related kidney damage
  • Acute kidney failure
  • End-stage kidney disease

Gastroenterology covers the evaluation, diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the stomach, intestines, liver, bile ducts and pancreas. The department at our partner hospital offers a wide range of diagnostic and therapeutic endoscopy, alongside dedicated care for reflux, liver disease, inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer screening. MedLuxLife helps you arrange procedures and understand preparation instructions; the hospital gives you your reports for your doctor at home.

Treatments and services

Diagnostic endoscopy

Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, colonoscopy and double-balloon endoscopy (enteroscopy), which can examine parts of the small intestine beyond the reach of standard scopes, for example in unexplained bleeding, iron-deficiency anaemia or suspected Crohn's disease.

Endoscopic treatment of bleeding

Band ligation, sclerotherapy, haemoclips and argon laser treatment for bleeding from the stomach or intestines.

Treatment of narrowing

Balloon dilatation and stent placement for strictures of the stomach or intestines.

Endoscopic obesity treatment

Intragastric balloon placement during upper endoscopy, which may support weight loss alongside lifestyle changes; the balloon is removed after a set period.

Reflux diagnosis and treatment

Upper endoscopy, 24-hour pH monitoring and motility studies, followed by medication, endoscopic options such as the Stretta procedure and endoscopic fundoplication (for example Plicator or Gastrofix), or surgery.

Helicobacter pylori testing

Urea breath test and stool antigen testing to diagnose H. pylori infection and guide treatment.

Colorectal cancer screening

Screening colonoscopy with polypectomy, as polyps can be found and removed during the procedure; people at higher risk receive an individual screening plan.

ERCP

Endoscopic imaging of the bile and pancreatic ducts, which also allows stone removal, stent placement to relieve blockages and biopsy.

Haemorrhoid treatment

Medication for early stages and band ligation, sclerotherapy, laser or infrared treatment during sedated colonoscopy for intermediate stages, with referral for surgery in advanced cases.

Hepatology unit

Diagnosis and long-term follow-up of chronic hepatitis B and C using liver function tests, HBV and HCV PCR, abdominal ultrasound and liver biopsy, with antiviral treatment options including interferon.

Inflammatory bowel disease

Diagnosis of ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease by colonoscopy and/or double-balloon enteroscopy, and ongoing medical treatment.

  • Polypectomy

  • HBV and HCV PCR tests

This multidisciplinary clinic is dedicated exclusively to diseases of the thyroid and parathyroid glands, offering early diagnosis together with medical and surgical treatment. Specialists from seven fields evaluate each case jointly, following current scientific evidence. MedLuxLife coordinates your assessment, tests and any surgery at our partner hospital, with clear communication at every stage.

Treatments and services

Multidisciplinary team

Specialists in endocrine surgery, endocrinology, nuclear medicine, radiology, pathology, genetics and bioengineering work together on each case.

Thyroid and parathyroid ultrasound

Dedicated ultrasound examination of the thyroid and parathyroid glands.

Scintigraphy

Thyroid (Tc99m), parathyroid (MIBI) and DOTATATE scintigraphy to assess gland function and locate abnormal tissue.

Choline PET

PET imaging that can help locate parathyroid tissue when other tests are inconclusive.

Function tests

Laboratory testing of thyroid and parathyroid hormone function.

Biopsy

Fine needle and Tru-Cut biopsy to examine nodules and suspicious tissue.

Radioactive iodine therapy

Radioactive iodine treatment for suitable thyroid conditions.

Lithium-supported radioactive iodine therapy

In selected cases, lithium may be used alongside radioactive iodine to support the treatment.

Radiofrequency ablation

Non-surgical treatment of thyroid nodules using radiofrequency energy.

Thyroid and parathyroid surgery

Operations using classical and microsurgical techniques, as well as the scarless transoral approach (TOETVA).

Parathyroid transplantation

Reimplantation of parathyroid tissue to help preserve gland function where needed.

  • Parathyroid transplantation

Endocrinology deals with the hormone-producing glands and the metabolic conditions they influence, such as diabetes, thyroid disorders and diseases of the pituitary and adrenal glands. Most of these conditions are diagnosed with blood tests and imaging and treated with medication and lifestyle measures, with long-term follow-up. MedLuxLife arranges a consultation with an endocrinologist at our partner hospital and coordinates any further tests or treatment.

For surgical treatment of the thyroid, parathyroid and adrenal glands, see Endocrine Surgery and the Thyroid and Parathyroid Clinic.

Treatments and services

Diabetes

Diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of type 1 and type 2 diabetes, including insulin therapy, modern oral and injectable medicines and screening for complications.

Thyroid disorders

Treatment of an underactive or overactive thyroid (hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism), Hashimoto's and Graves' disease, and assessment of thyroid nodules.

Pituitary diseases

Diagnosis and treatment of pituitary tumours and hormone imbalances, in cooperation with the pituitary clinic and neurosurgery.

Adrenal diseases

Assessment of adrenal gland disorders such as Cushing's syndrome, Addison's disease, hyperaldosteronism and adrenal masses.

Calcium, bone and parathyroid

Diagnosis and treatment of osteoporosis, vitamin D deficiency and parathyroid hormone disorders.

Obesity and metabolic syndrome

Medical assessment of weight-related metabolic problems, insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome, with referral to nutrition or obesity surgery where suitable.

Lipid disorders

Diagnosis and treatment of high cholesterol and triglyceride levels to reduce cardiovascular risk.

Reproductive hormones

Hormonal causes of irregular periods, hirsutism, PCOS, low testosterone and menopause-related complaints.

Tests and examinations

  • Hormone blood tests
  • Dynamic hormone stimulation and suppression tests
  • Oral glucose tolerance test and HbA1c
  • Thyroid ultrasound
  • Fine-needle aspiration biopsy of thyroid nodules
  • Bone density measurement (DEXA)
  • Imaging of the pituitary and adrenal glands in cooperation with radiology

Endocrine surgery treats disorders of the hormone-producing glands, mainly the thyroid, parathyroid and adrenal glands, when too much or too little hormone is produced or when a growth needs removal. These delicate operations require careful technique to protect the voice, calcium balance and surrounding structures. MedLuxLife arranges your consultation with the surgical team at our partner hospital and plans your stay around surgery and recovery; hormone results and scans go directly to the doctors.

Treatments and services

Thyroidectomy

Removal of the whole thyroid gland or one of its lobes, for example for nodules, goitre, overactivity or cancer.

Parathyroidectomy

Removal of one or more of the four parathyroid glands, which regulate calcium and phosphorus levels.

Parathyroid transplantation

Reimplantation of parathyroid tissue, which may be performed to preserve calcium regulation.

Adrenalectomy

Removal of one or both adrenal glands, which produce cortisol and hormones involved in blood pressure control and development.

Pancreatectomy

Removal of part or all of the pancreas, for example for neuroendocrine tumours.

Specialised surgical expertise

Operations are carried out by surgeons with additional experience in endocrine surgery, with a focus on careful, precise technique.

Conditions treated surgically

  • Cushing's syndrome
  • Parathyroid gland disorders

  • Parathyroid cancer
  • Hyperparathyroidism
  • Hyperthyroidism
  • Goitre
  • Graves' disease
  • Toxic (hyperfunctioning) thyroid nodules
  • Thyroid nodules
  • Thyroid cancer
  • Neuroendocrine tumours

Audiology covers the detailed assessment and rehabilitation of hearing and balance problems in babies, children and adults. The department at our partner hospital offers a broad range of hearing and vestibular tests, including objective tests suitable for infants and for people with dizziness. MedLuxLife helps families schedule tests at suitable times, explains preparation requirements in advance and arranges for results to be shared with your doctors at home.

Treatments and services

Newborn hearing screening

Screening of babies' hearing using BERA so that possible hearing loss can be identified early.

Clinical BERA (ABR)

An objective electrophysiological test that measures the auditory nerve's response to sound through electrodes placed on the head, used especially for infants who did not pass screening, babies with risk factors and children with speech delay who cannot complete other tests. It is also known as ABR, BAEP or BAER.

Clinical otoacoustic emissions and ASSR

TEOAE/DPOAE and auditory steady-state response testing, which can support and complement BERA findings.

Child audiometry

Age-appropriate hearing tests including behavioural observation audiometry, visual reinforcement audiometry and play audiometry, as well as free field testing.

Adult hearing evaluation

Pure-tone and speech audiometry, plus high-frequency audiometry where indicated.

Middle ear and Eustachian tube tests

Tympanometry and acoustic reflex testing, high-frequency (1000 Hz) tympanometry for babies up to six months, and Eustachian tube function testing.

Videonystagmography (VNG)

Records eye movements with video goggles during oculomotor, positional and caloric tests to help determine whether dizziness originates in the inner ear or the brain.

Video head impulse test (vHIT)

Assesses the vestibulo-ocular reflex of each semicircular canal separately.

VEMP test

Vestibular evoked myogenic potentials, used in the differential diagnosis of conditions such as semicircular canal dehiscence, early Meniere's disease and otolith organ dysfunction.

Caloric and rotational testing

Caloric vestibular testing (ENG) and rotational examination to evaluate the function of each balance organ and central compensation.

Repositioning manoeuvres for BPPV

When benign paroxysmal positional vertigo is identified, corrective manoeuvres such as Epley, Vannucchi, Gufoni and BBQ roll may be performed.

Preparing a child for BERA

The test is usually done during natural sleep without medication, so babies are brought awake and fasted for feeding and sleep at the clinic; evening appointments, or testing under general anaesthesia with an anaesthetist at the family's request, may be arranged.

Conditions that tests can help evaluate

  • Hearing loss in babies, children and adults
  • Speech and language delay with suspected hearing loss
  • Dizziness and balance disorders
  • Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV)
  • Vestibular neuronitis
  • Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO)
  • Balance problems after traumatic brain injury
  • Semicircular canal dehiscence
  • Meniere's disease
  • Otolith organ-related vestibular dysfunction

Breast surgery deals with the surgical treatment of breast diseases, most notably breast cancer, where early diagnosis can make a meaningful difference to treatment options. At our partner hospital, breast surgeons work alongside medical oncology, plastic surgery, radiology and pathology so that each plan reflects the individual's diagnosis and preferences. MedLuxLife helps you gather your imaging and biopsy results and arranges a multidisciplinary opinion before any decision is made.

Treatments and services

Multidisciplinary breast care

Diagnosis and treatment planning involve breast surgery, medical oncology, plastic surgery, radiology, pathology and other specialists as needed.

Lumpectomy (breast-conserving surgery)

Removal of the tumour together with a small margin of surrounding healthy tissue, preserving the rest of the breast.

Total mastectomy

Removal of the entire breast, which may be considered in early- or later-stage breast cancer depending on the individual situation.

Nipple-sparing mastectomy

Removal of breast tissue while preserving the skin and nipple, usually combined with an implant to restore breast shape.

Prophylactic mastectomy

Preventive removal of breast tissue that may be discussed with people at high risk of breast cancer to help reduce that risk.

Individual choice of technique

The surgical approach is selected according to the stage of disease, the patient's condition and their wishes.

Chronic pelvic pain can affect every part of daily life, and finding its cause often requires more than one specialist. This multidisciplinary clinic investigates the nature and origin of pelvic pain, including endometriosis, using diagnostic methods chosen according to each patient's symptoms, and then plans treatment based on current medical evidence. MedLuxLife arranges your evaluation at our partner hospital and supports you with preparation, records and travel.

Treatments and services

Detailed pain assessment

A structured consultation explores when, where and how the pain occurs, its intensity and its effect on work and daily life.

Symptom-based diagnostics

Diagnostic methods are selected to match each patient's symptoms in order to identify the cause of the pain.

Endometriosis evaluation

Assessment of endometriosis as a possible cause of pelvic pain, followed by individual treatment planning.

Multidisciplinary team

Women's health specialists work together with urology, gastroenterology, general surgery, physical therapy and psychiatry.

Individual treatment planning

Treatment is planned in line with current developments, with the aim of improving quality of life affected by pain.

Psychological wellbeing

Mood and emotional strain are considered as part of the overall assessment, with psychiatric input available where helpful.

Questions your consultation may cover

  • When the pain first started and how often it occurs
  • Where and when the pain appears, and whether it stays in one place
  • How long each episode lasts
  • Whether the pain has changed or spread over time
  • How intense the pain is on a scale of 1 to 10
  • Whether the pain limits your ability to work
  • Any link to the menstrual cycle, urination or sexual intercourse
  • How you would describe the pain (sharp, dull, aching)

  • Any connection with eating, sleeping, sex or movement

  • Anything that eases or worsens the pain
  • Any previous pelvic surgery
  • Any previous treatment for urinary tract or vaginal infections

Perinatology, a division of obstetrics and gynaecology, focuses on the health of mother and baby during pregnancy. Alongside routine pregnancy care and delivery, it provides follow-up and management of high-risk pregnancies and the diagnosis and management of maternal and fetal conditions using specialised scans, tests and procedures. MedLuxLife helps expectant parents arrange screening, specialist scans and consultations at our partner hospital and coordinates every step of the visit.

Treatments and services

Routine and high-risk pregnancy care

Pregnancy follow-up and delivery, with closer monitoring and management for high-risk pregnancies.

First-trimester screening (11-14 weeks)

An ultrasound nuchal translucency measurement, which can be combined with blood tests and further markers such as the fetal nasal bone, blood flow in the fetal heart and the facial angle, to assess the risk of Down syndrome and other conditions.

Second-trimester screening (15-21 weeks)

A triple or quadruple blood test that estimates risk; a raised result indicates that diagnostic testing may be advisable, not that the baby is affected.

Early detailed anomaly scan (11-14 weeks)

A detailed transvaginal ultrasound examination of fetal development early in pregnancy.

Detailed anomaly scan (18-22 weeks)

A high-resolution second-level ultrasound examining fetal organs and growth, which can include uterine artery Doppler and cervical length assessment in at-risk pregnancies.

Fetal echocardiography

A detailed examination of the baby's heart structure and function, recommended when there is an increased risk of congenital heart disease or a suspected abnormality; ideally performed around 18-21 weeks.

Doppler ultrasound

Maternal and fetal Doppler examinations to assess blood flow to the placenta and within the baby's circulation.

Chorionic villus sampling (CVS)

A placental tissue sample, usually taken at 11-14 weeks under ultrasound guidance, to examine chromosome number and structure.

Amniocentesis

A small sample of amniotic fluid, usually taken at 16-22 weeks, for chromosomal analysis; rapid FISH testing for selected chromosomes may give preliminary results sooner.

Cordocentesis (fetal blood sampling)

A small blood sample from the umbilical cord vein, usually after the 19th week, for diagnostic testing.

Counselling and birth planning

Results are discussed with parents, and findings such as a heart abnormality help plan where and how the birth should take place.

Tests and procedures

  • 11-14 week screening tests
  • 15-21 week screening tests (triple or quadruple test)
  • 11-14 week transvaginal detailed fetal anomaly screening
  • 18-22 week obstetric detailed anomaly screening
  • Fetal echocardiography
  • Maternal and fetal Doppler ultrasonography
  • Uterine artery Doppler
  • Cervical length assessment
  • Chorionic villus sampling (CVS)
  • Amniocentesis, including FISH analysis
  • Fetal blood sampling (cordocentesis)

Investigation of recurrent pregnancy loss and repeated unsuccessful IVF attempts.

Support during menopause, including mammography, bone density measurement and psychological counselling in cooperation with radiology and psychiatry.

Learning that kidney damage is permanent can be a difficult moment, and careful confirmation of the diagnosis comes first. The kidney transplant team at our partner hospital aims to protect kidney function for as long as possible and, where kidney failure reaches its final stage, assesses whether a transplant is a suitable option. MedLuxLife coordinates the evaluation for both recipient and donor, organises appointments and travel, and supports you through follow-up.

Treatments and services

Protecting kidney function

Nephrologists evaluate, treat and follow patients with declining kidney function, aiming to slow damage and, where possible, reverse it.

Confirming the diagnosis

Examination, tests, imaging and medical history are reviewed carefully to establish whether kidney damage is irreversible.

Transplant suitability assessment

A systematic review of all organ systems, with particular attention to heart and blood vessel health, to identify any reasons a transplant may not be advisable.

Managing other health conditions

Coexisting conditions found during the assessment are treated before transplantation is planned.

Living donor transplantation

For suitable patients, a kidney may be transplanted from a living donor following assessment.

Deceased donor transplantation

Transplantation from a deceased donor is the alternative option for suitable patients.

Algology, or pain medicine, focuses on identifying the source of chronic pain and building a treatment plan around the individual, including pain whose cause is difficult to pin down. At our partner hospital, a pain specialist examines each patient in detail before recommending options, which may combine medical, interventional and lifestyle measures. MedLuxLife arranges the consultation, shares your records in advance and coordinates any follow-up.

Treatments and services

Chronic pain treatment

Assessment and personalised management of long-standing pain, with the aim of finding its underlying cause.

Interventional pain treatment

Image-guided and needle-based procedures that target the structures thought to be generating pain.

Cancer pain management

Pain control tailored to people living with cancer, coordinated with their wider treatment.

Acupuncture (dry needling)

A needle-based therapy that may be used alongside other approaches to help relieve muscular and chronic pain.

Ozone therapy

Medical ozone treatment, including autohaemotherapy, offered as part of selected pain treatment plans.

Epiduroscopy

A minimally invasive endoscopic examination of the epidural space that can be used in the assessment and treatment of certain back and leg pain.

Epidural steroid injection

Injection of medication into the epidural space, which may help reduce inflammation-related spinal and radiating pain.

Regional and sympathetic nerve blocks

Targeted injections that interrupt pain signals along specific nerves or the sympathetic nervous system, which may provide longer-term relief in suitable patients.

Radiofrequency thermocoagulation

Controlled heat delivered by radio waves to selected nerves to reduce the transmission of pain.

Pain conditions treated

  • Cancer pain
  • Headaches
  • Facial pain and neuralgia
  • Neck pain
  • Shoulder and arm pain
  • Back pain
  • Lower back and leg pain
  • Pain due to vascular occlusion
  • Pain of unknown origin

Interventional radiology uses imaging such as ultrasound, CT and angiography to guide minimally invasive diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Interventional radiologists not only diagnose disease but also take an active part in its treatment, often through a small puncture rather than open surgery. MedLuxLife coordinates your assessment at our partner hospital, including pre-procedure tests, and supports you through recovery and travel home.

Treatments and services

Image-guided biopsies

Fine-needle aspiration and Tru-cut biopsies guided by ultrasound and/or CT for the neck and thyroid, chest, abdominal organs and bones.

Diagnostic angiography

Contrast imaging of arteries, usually via the femoral artery, with high-resolution and 3D imaging to show even small vessel branches.

Venography

Imaging of veins to investigate thrombosis, tumour blockages and adrenal tumours, or to assess the saphenous vein before bypass surgery.

Chest procedures

Non-vascular interventions such as thoracentesis, abscess drainage and stenting of tracheobronchial narrowing.

Abdominal, biliary and kidney procedures

Biliary drainage and stenting, nephrostomy, ureteral stenting, cyst and abscess drainage and RF ablation.

Arterial angioplasty and stenting

Balloon and stent treatment of narrowed or blocked arteries throughout the body, from the carotid and brain vessels to the legs.

Neurointerventional treatment

Coil embolisation of brain aneurysms, embolisation of AVMs and fistulas, and intra-arterial thrombolysis in acute stroke within a limited time window.

Embolisation for bleeding and tumours

Embolisation for nosebleeds, coughing up blood and acute gastrointestinal bleeding, and for head and neck tumours.

Aortic and peripheral endografts

Covered stents for aneurysms of the thoracic and abdominal aorta and for pseudoaneurysms in peripheral arteries.

Oncological interventions

Transarterial chemoembolisation and RF ablation for liver tumours, portal vein interventions and venous port placement.

Venous and dialysis access

Venous angioplasty and stenting, dialysis catheters, fistula angioplasty, vena cava filters, TIPS and venous catheters.

Uterine fibroid embolisation and diabetic foot

Fibroid embolisation as an alternative to surgery, and balloon and laser angioplasty for narrowed foot vessels in diabetes.

The department at our partner hospital offers surgery for both adults and children, with dedicated intensive care and a sterile operating environment. Coronary bypass surgery

Heart valve surgery

Aortic surgery

Surgery for aortic aneurysms of the ascending aorta, arch and descending aorta, including combined procedures, and for acute and chronic aortic dissection.

Surgical treatment of diseases affecting the arteries and veins outside the heart.

Removal of the pericardium, the sac around the heart, when it restricts heart function.

Nuclear medicine uses small amounts of radioactive substances to image and treat disease at a molecular level, giving information about how organs function as well as how they look. The department at our partner hospital works with many specialties, including cardiology, nephrology, orthopaedics, oncology and endocrinology, and has been designed to keep radiation exposure for patients and staff to a minimum. MedLuxLife coordinates referrals, scan appointments and the transfer of results to your treating doctors.

Treatments and services

Neurological applications

Scans that can support the diagnosis of certain strokes, dementia and hydrocephalus, and help locate the seizure focus before epilepsy surgery.

Lung applications

Imaging to investigate pulmonary embolism and to estimate remaining lung function before lung surgery.

Orthopaedic applications

Bone imaging to reveal hidden fractures, bone infection and bone metastases.

Heart applications

Studies to assess coronary artery disease and to evaluate the heart after bypass surgery or stenting.

Kidney applications

Imaging to look for urinary tract obstruction, urine reflux towards the kidneys and kidney infection, and to support kidney transplantation.

Oncology applications

Scans that help distinguish benign from malignant lesions, stage tumours, guide biopsy sites, detect recurrence, assess response to chemotherapy and plan radiotherapy.

Other diagnostic studies

Investigations of goitre, oesophageal, stomach and gallbladder disease, acute intestinal bleeding, hidden infection, lymphatic drainage, tear ducts and salivary gland function.

Patient-focused design

Spacious rooms, zoned layout according to radiation levels and daylight-style lighting in treatment rooms are intended to support comfort and safety.

Clinical applications

  • Diagnosis of certain strokes
  • Diagnosis of dementia
  • Locating the epileptic focus before epilepsy surgery
  • Diagnosis of hydrocephalus
  • Diagnosis of pulmonary embolism (lung clot)
  • Assessment of lung reserve before lung surgery
  • Visualising hidden fractures
  • Bone infections
  • Imaging of bone metastases
  • Diagnosis of coronary artery disease
  • Evaluation after bypass surgery or stent placement
  • Visualising urinary tract obstruction
  • Investigating urine reflux to the kidneys
  • Investigating kidney infections
  • Kidney transplantation
  • Differentiating benign from malignant lesions
  • Staging of tumours
  • Identifying the biopsy site
  • Detecting tumour recurrence
  • Evaluating response to chemotherapy
  • Radiotherapy planning
  • Goitre
  • Oesophageal and stomach diseases
  • Gallbladder diseases
  • Acute intestinal bleeding
  • Suspected hidden infection
  • Examination of lymphatic pathways
  • Examination of the tear ducts
  • Assessment of salivary gland function

Bone marrow (stem cell) transplantation is a complex, multi-stage treatment that calls for close teamwork between laboratories, clinical units and nursing staff. The transplant clinic at our partner hospital brings these stages together under one roof, from diagnostic work-up and treatment planning to follow-up after discharge. MedLuxLife helps adult patients and their families arrange the evaluation with the specialists and stay well informed throughout a lengthy treatment journey.

Treatments and services

Transplant outpatient clinic

Coordinates assessment, decision-making, treatment and follow-up for patients who are being considered for, or are undergoing, a transplant, reviewing previous treatment, imaging, pathology and laboratory findings together.

Apheresis unit

Collects stem cells from the blood as part of the transplant process.

Stem cell freezing and processing

Processes stem cells and stores them cryogenically in nitrogen tanks, with separate quarantine and main storage, using an automated freezing system.

Flow cytometry laboratory

Analyses blood and marrow cells to support diagnosis, treatment planning and assessment of the response to treatment.

HLA tissue typing laboratory

Performs tissue typing used to assess compatibility between patient and donor.

Genetic diagnostic support

Works alongside a genetic diagnosis centre so that genetic findings can inform diagnosis and treatment decisions.

Protected transplant unit

Treatment takes place in single rooms within a dedicated unit with HEPA air filtration throughout, controlled disinfection on entry and beds that can be converted for emergency care.

Comfort and wellbeing

Rooms are designed with views and patient comfort in mind to support psychological wellbeing during a long hospital stay.

Follow-up before and after transplant

Patients are monitored closely at every stage, and follow-up continues after discharge with the involvement of social support teams.

At our partner hospital's neurological sciences centre, neurosurgeons work in a multidisciplinary team with neurologists, anaesthesiologists, intensive care specialists, radiologists, psychiatrists, psychologists and rehabilitation specialists, in specialised wards and intensive care units.

Treatments and services

Neuro-oncology

Microsurgical treatment of tumours of the brain, spinal cord and nerve sheaths, pituitary tumours and skull base tumours.

Neurovascular surgery

Treatment of aneurysms, subarachnoid haemorrhage, arteriovenous malformations of the brain and spinal cord and selected strokes, including bypass surgery for blocked brain vessels.

Epilepsy surgery

Surgical treatment of epilepsy by a specialised neurology and neurosurgery team, including epilepsy monitoring.

Spine and spinal cord surgery

Surgery for lumbar and cervical disc herniation, age-related spinal stenosis and wear, spinal and spinal cord tumours and congenital disorders.

Kyphoplasty and vertebroplasty

Spine-strengthening procedures for fractures caused by osteoporosis or tumour metastases.

Pain and spasticity treatment

Intrathecal drug pumps for spasticity and pain, and injection treatments for spine-related pain that does not need surgery.

Peripheral nerve surgery

Microsurgical treatment of carpal tunnel syndrome, ulnar and peroneal nerve compression, meralgia paraesthetica and nerve or plexus injuries.

Stereotactic and functional neurosurgery

Precise, image-guided procedures on the brain.

Neurospinal trauma

Treatment of injuries of the brain, spine and spinal cord.

Paediatric neurosurgery

Surgical treatment of brain and spine conditions in children.

The wish to have a child is very personal. Our partner IVF centre plans every treatment individually, based on current scientific evidence, and its experienced team of physicians and embryologists decides together on each case. The causes of infertility are investigated carefully first, so that you are spared unnecessary treatment.

Treatments and services

Fertility assessment

Medical history, ultrasound, hormone tests, semen analysis and, if needed, hysteroscopy for both partners.

IVF treatment

Ovarian stimulation over about 8 to 14 days, egg collection under anaesthesia, fertilisation in the laboratory and a painless embryo transfer.

Natural (drug-free) IVF

IVF in your natural cycle without stimulating medication, for example for women who respond poorly to medication or prefer not to use hormones.

Intrauterine insemination (IUI)

Prepared sperm are placed directly into the uterus around ovulation.

Microinjection (ICSI)

A single sperm is injected into each egg; used for male-factor infertility, including cases with no sperm in the semen (azoospermia).

Microchip sperm selection

Sperm with better motility and quality are selected using a microfluidic chip before fertilisation.

Egg freezing (cryopreservation)

Eggs or embryos are frozen for later use, for example before chemotherapy or radiotherapy or to postpone pregnancy.

Co-culture

Embryos are cultured together with supporting cells to support their development in the laboratory.

Assisted hatching

The outer shell of the embryo is gently thinned or opened to help implantation, for example after repeated unsuccessful transfers.

Preimplantation genetic diagnosis (PGD)

Embryos can be tested when a parent carries a hereditary disease, so that healthy embryos are selected.

Ovarian rejuvenation (PRP)

A treatment option that may be considered for selected women with low ovarian reserve.

Difficult cases

Special protocols for advanced age, low ovarian reserve, PCOS, endometriosis and repeated IVF failure.

Orthopaedics and traumatology deal with the diagnosis, treatment and rehabilitation of problems of the bones, joints, muscles and spine in adults and children, including injuries from daily life and sport. Our partner hospital combines experienced orthopaedic surgeons with robotic and navigation technology and works with physical therapy and rehabilitation for a quick return to daily life.

Treatments and services

Arthroscopic surgery

Closed (keyhole) surgery of the knee, shoulder, hip, ankle, elbow and wrist. Recovery is quick and in many cases no hospital stay is needed.

Robotic joint replacement

Joint replacement for arthritis performed with robotic technology, special navigation systems and computer assistance.

Knee, hip and shoulder replacement

Joint prostheses for advanced joint wear, for pain-free movement.

Sports injuries

Treatment of ligament, meniscus, tendon and cartilage injuries from sport.

Foot and ankle

Treatment of foot and ankle injuries and conditions.

Shoulder surgery

Surgical treatment of shoulder injuries, instability and wear.

Cartilage transplantation

For extensive cartilage damage where other treatments have failed, to preserve the joint and prevent or delay the need for a prosthesis.

Biological cartilage treatments

Biological (orthobiological) treatment of cartilage diseases.

Spine surgery

Treatment of spinal fractures, infections, tumours and congenital or acquired curvatures.

Fracture and trauma care

Treatment of fractures and injuries and their consequences.

Paediatric orthopaedics

Diagnosis and treatment of orthopaedic problems in children.

Orthopaedic oncology

Diagnosis and treatment of bone and soft tissue tumours.

Cardiology covers the evaluation, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of heart conditions. Our partner hospital's cardiology department includes a cardiology outpatient clinic, a coronary intensive care unit, cardiac catheterisation and angiography laboratories, an electrophysiology unit and cardiology laboratories, and works closely with cardiovascular surgery.

Treatments and services

Echocardiography

Transthoracic and transoesophageal echocardiography to assess the structure and function of the heart.

Stress and rhythm tests

Treadmill stress test, rhythm Holter, event recorder and tilt-table test.

Blood pressure monitoring

24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring.

Coronary angiography and catheterisation

Coronary angiography, haemodynamic studies and right and left heart catheterisation.

Coronary angioplasty and stents

Percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA) and intracoronary stent placement.

Pacemakers and ICDs

Implantation of permanent pacemakers and implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICD).

Electrophysiology and RF ablation

Electrophysiological studies and radiofrequency ablation to treat heart rhythm disorders.

Balloon valvuloplasty

Mitral and pulmonary balloon valvuloplasty to widen narrowed heart valves.

Catheter closure of heart defects

Percutaneous closure of atrial septal defects (ASD) and patent ductus arteriosus (PDA).

Other interventional procedures

Septal ablation, pericardiocentesis and endomyocardial biopsy.

Cancer treatment is planned according to the type, stage and biological features of the disease and your personal situation. Through our partner hospital, your case is assessed by a multidisciplinary team in which medical oncologists work closely with surgeons, radiation oncologists and other specialists.

Treatments and services

Personal treatment planning

A treatment plan tailored to the type and stage of the disease, agreed in cooperation with surgery, radiation oncology and other departments.

Chemotherapy

Drug treatments that stop the growth of cancer cells or destroy them, planned individually.

Targeted therapy

Medicines that act on specific features of cancer cells, used where the tumour biology makes them suitable.

Immunotherapy

Treatments that help the immune system to recognise and fight cancer cells.

Hormone therapy

Used for hormone-sensitive cancers, such as some breast and prostate cancers.

Follow-up and supportive care

Regular follow-up, management of side effects, preserving quality of life and psychosocial support during treatment.

Bariatric (obesity) surgery can lead to substantial, lasting weight loss and improve weight-related health problems and quality of life. The right procedure depends on your health, your weight and your goals, and is chosen together with your surgeon.

A supportive, respectful approach

Deciding on weight-loss surgery is a big step, and you do not have to take it alone. We take your health, your dignity and your well-being seriously and work with experienced teams who offer evidence-based treatment in a supportive, judgement-free setting.

Weight-loss treatments

Gastric Sleeve

Sleeve gastrectomy reduces the size of the stomach, which limits food intake and leads to significant, sustainable weight loss. One of the most widely performed weight-loss operations today.

Free consultation →

Gastric Bypass

The most common form, the Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, reduces food intake and limits calorie absorption by changing the route of the digestive tract. A proven option for long-term weight loss.

Free consultation →

Gastric Balloon

A non-surgical option: a soft, saline-filled balloon is placed in the stomach in a short procedure of about 20 minutes, without an operation. It creates a feeling of fullness and helps to reduce food intake; depending on the balloon system, it is passed naturally after a few months or removed endoscopically. On average it leads to a weight loss of about 10% of body weight and is often a first step on the weight-loss journey.

Free consultation →

Medical aesthetics offers non-surgical treatments to smooth lines, restore volume and refresh the skin, with little or no downtime. Treatments are carried out by qualified doctors and planned to keep your natural expression.

Medical aesthetic treatments

Botox (Botulinum Toxin)

Relaxes the muscles that cause expression lines – forehead lines, frown lines, crow's feet, lines around the lips, at the corners of the mouth and on the nose (bunny lines) – and neck bands. It can also be used for a subtle brow lift.

Medical uses include reducing excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis) and easing jaw tension related to teeth grinding.

Free consultation →

Dermal Fillers

Hyaluronic acid fillers restore volume and smooth folds. The effect is visible straight away and usually lasts about 6–18 months, depending on the product. Common areas:

  • Nasolabial folds (smile lines)
  • Cheeks and temples
  • Lips: volume, definition and hydration
  • Chin and jawline contouring

Free consultation →

Skin Mesotherapy

Micro-injections deliver vitamins, minerals, amino acids and other nourishing substances directly into the skin, for skin rejuvenation, cellulite or localised fat. Several sessions give the best results; downtime is minimal.

Free consultation →

Exosome Skin Treatments

Exosomes deliver growth factors and proteins to skin cells to support regeneration and collagen production. Applied after microneedling, laser or radiofrequency treatments, they help the skin recover and look brighter, firmer and smoother.

Free consultation →

PRP (Platelet-Rich Plasma)

A small amount of your own blood is processed in a centrifuge to obtain plasma rich in platelets and growth factors. Applied to or injected into the skin, it supports collagen production and skin regeneration. PRP is also used on the scalp for thinning hair.

Free consultation →

Microneedling

Very fine, sterile needles create tiny controlled channels in the top layer of the skin, which stimulates the production of new collagen and elastin. Used for acne scars, enlarged pores and uneven skin texture – often combined with PRP or serums.

Free consultation →

Plastic and aesthetic surgery can restore harmony and proportion to the face and body. MedLuxLife connects you with experienced plastic surgeons and plans every step of your stay, from the first consultation to your recovery, so you can make your decision calmly and with full information.

Plastic surgery procedures

Mommy Makeover

A combination of procedures that addresses changes after pregnancy and childbirth, tailored to your needs. It may include:

  • Tummy tuck to remove excess skin and tighten the abdominal muscles
  • Breast lift or augmentation to restore shape and volume
  • Liposuction for stubborn fat on the abdomen, hips or thighs
  • Intimate rejuvenation, such as labiaplasty

Learn more →

Rhinoplasty

Reshapes the nose to improve facial balance and, where needed, breathing.

  • Cosmetic rhinoplasty: changes size, tip shape or nostrils, or corrects asymmetry
  • Functional rhinoplasty (septorhinoplasty): improves breathing, for example with a deviated septum

Learn more →

Abdominoplasty (Tummy Tuck)

Removes excess skin and fat from the abdomen and tightens the underlying muscles for a flatter, firmer contour.

  • Full abdominoplasty: an incision from hip to hip, often with repositioning of the navel
  • Mini abdominoplasty: a shorter incision for minor excess below the navel

Learn more →

Breast Augmentation

Increases breast size and volume or restores volume lost after weight changes or pregnancy, using silicone or saline implants or your own fat. Implant type, size and incision site are chosen with your surgeon.

Learn more →

Breast Reduction

Reduces the size and weight of very large breasts. It can relieve back and neck pain, restricted movement and skin irritation, and creates a more balanced silhouette.

Learn more →

Gynecomastia Surgery

Male breast reduction removes excess glandular tissue and fat, using liposuction, direct excision or both, for a flatter, more masculine chest.

Learn more →

Brachioplasty (Arm Lift)

Removes loose skin and fat from the upper arms, often after major weight loss or with age, through an incision on the inner or back of the arm.

Learn more →

Brazilian Butt Lift (BBL)

Fat is removed by liposuction from areas such as the abdomen or flanks, purified and transferred to the buttocks for more volume and a natural, lifted shape.

Learn more →

Thigh Lift

Removes excess skin and fat from the thighs and tightens the tissue for a smoother contour, typically after significant weight loss.

Learn more →

Blepharoplasty (Eyelid Surgery)

Corrects drooping upper eyelids and under-eye bags for a fresher, more youthful look. Upper eyelid surgery is usually done under local anaesthesia; lower eyelid surgery generally under general anaesthesia.

Learn more →

Facelift

Reduces visible signs of ageing such as sagging skin and deep folds. Depending on your needs, the surgeon chooses a full, mini, mid-face or temporal lift.

Learn more →

Buccal Fat Removal

Reduces the fat pads in the lower cheeks through small incisions inside the mouth, for more sculpted cheeks and a defined jawline. Usually performed under local anaesthesia.

Learn more →

Liposuction

Removes stubborn fat deposits that do not respond to diet and exercise, for example on the abdomen, thighs, arms, back or waist, to sculpt the body contour.

Learn more →

Breast Lift (Mastopexy)

Lifts and reshapes sagging breasts for a firmer, more youthful position. It can be combined with augmentation to add volume at the same time.

Learn more →

Otoplasty (Ear Correction)

Reshapes or repositions prominent or asymmetric ears. Possible for adults and for children from about 5–6 years of age, once the ears have finished growing.

Learn more →

Neck Lift

Tightens loose skin and reshapes the neck and jawline. Often combined with a facelift for a harmonious result.

Hair transplantation moves healthy hair follicles from areas where hair is resistant to thinning, usually the back and sides of the head, to areas with thinning or hair loss. It is one of the most requested aesthetic procedures for men and women with pattern hair loss, and the results grow naturally with your own hair.

Hair transplantation treatments

Hair and Scalp Analysis

Before any treatment, an AI-supported digital analysis evaluates hair density and thickness, the health of individual follicles and whether they are in a growth or resting phase. This helps to choose the most suitable technique and to track your progress objectively over time.

Free consultation →

FUE (Follicular Unit Extraction)

Individual follicles are taken one by one from the donor area with a fine, circular micro-punch and implanted into the thinning areas. No linear scar, and a comfortable recovery.

Learn more →

Beard and Moustache Transplant

For a fuller, more defined beard or moustache. Follicles, usually from the back of the head, are transplanted into sparse areas. An effective option for uneven growth, scarring or hair loss caused by genetics, hormones or injury.

Learn more →

Eyebrow Transplant

Reshapes and strengthens thin, sparse or over-plucked eyebrows with your own hair follicles. A permanent, natural-looking alternative to make-up or microblading.

Learn more →

Sapphire FUE

An advanced form of FUE in which the channels are opened with blades made of sapphire crystal instead of steel. The finer, sharper blades allow very precise incisions, with less tissue trauma and swelling.

Free consultation →

DHI (Direct Hair Implantation)

Follicles are implanted directly with a special implanter pen (Choi pen), without opening channels in advance. This allows precise control of angle, direction and depth.

Learn more →

FUT (Follicular Unit Transplantation)

A strip of skin is taken from the donor area and divided into individual follicular units. FUT allows many grafts in one session but leaves a longer linear scar, so it is used today only in selected cases.

Free consultation →

Restorative Hair Therapies

Not every case of thinning hair needs surgery. Restorative hair therapies nourish and stimulate the hair follicles, help to slow hair loss and improve hair density and quality. They can be used on their own or to support the results of a hair transplant.

Exosome Therapy

Exosomes are tiny vesicles released by cells that carry proteins, lipids and growth signals. For hair restoration they are usually derived from mesenchymal stem cells and injected into thinning areas of the scalp, where they stimulate the follicles, extend the growth phase and support a healthier scalp. Exosomes are often combined with PRP.

Free consultation →

Hair Mesotherapy

A tailored blend of vitamins, amino acids, plant extracts and other active ingredients is injected into the scalp to nourish the hair follicles. Usually performed as a series of sessions; many patients notice thicker, stronger hair over time.

A motorised mesotherapy device delivers even micro-injections at a controlled depth, which makes the treatment quicker and more comfortable than manual injections.

Free consultation →

Red Light Therapy

A non-invasive, low-level light treatment at wavelengths of around 600 to 650 nanometres. The light is absorbed by the follicle cells, stimulates their energy production, improves local circulation and supports healthy hair growth.

Free consultation →

PRP (Platelet-Rich Plasma)

A small amount of your own blood is processed in a centrifuge to obtain plasma rich in platelets. Injected into the scalp, it stimulates the hair follicles and supports cell renewal. PRP is a well-established option to reduce hair loss and improve hair density.

Free consultation →

A healthy, natural-looking smile supports both your well-being and your confidence. MedLuxLife connects you with experienced dental specialists who combine modern digital diagnostics with proven treatment methods, from a single implant to a complete smile makeover.

Dental treatments

Hollywood Smile

A complete smile makeover designed to create a bright, even and harmonious smile that suits your facial features. Depending on your needs, it can combine:

  • Teeth whitening for an even, natural brightness
  • Veneers in porcelain or zirconium to correct discolouration, chips or minor misalignment
  • Dental bonding to repair small flaws or gaps
  • Contouring and reshaping for symmetry and balance
  • Gum contouring for an even gum line

Learn more →

Dental Implants

Dental implants replace missing teeth. A titanium or other biocompatible implant is placed in the jawbone, where it integrates over time and forms a stable base for a crown, bridge or denture.

  • Looks and feels like a natural tooth
  • Restores full chewing function
  • Long-lasting with proper care
  • Helps preserve the jawbone

Learn more →

All-on-4 and All-on-6

Fixed full-arch solutions for patients who are missing most or all of their teeth. A complete set of upper or lower teeth is supported by four or six implants. In many cases temporary teeth can be fitted on the same day.

All-on-6 may be recommended where more stability is needed or bone loss is more advanced. Your dentist will advise which option suits you.

Learn more →

Prosthetic Dental Treatments

Aesthetic and functional solutions for missing teeth, including fixed crowns and bridges placed over natural teeth.

Free consultation →

Implant-Supported Prostheses

Fixed or removable prostheses attached to implants in the jawbone, offering better stability and comfort than conventional dentures.

Free consultation →

Teeth Whitening

A cosmetic treatment that lightens the colour of the teeth and removes stains and discolouration.

Learn more →

Zirconium Veneers

Custom-made restorations in zirconia ceramic that improve the shape and colour of your teeth while looking natural.

  • Very strong and resistant to chipping and staining
  • If you grind your teeth, the dentist will check whether veneers are suitable for you
  • Metal-free and hypoallergenic

Learn more →

Periodontology (Gum Treatment)

Healthy teeth need healthy gums. Gum inflammation (gingivitis) and advanced gum disease (periodontitis) are treated with professional cleaning, scaling and root planing and, where necessary, surgical procedures to protect the gums and bone.

Free consultation →

Restorative Dental Treatments

Repair of damaged or decayed teeth, for example with fillings, to restore their function, structure and appearance.

Free consultation →

Root Canal Treatment

Removing inflamed or damaged pulp, then cleaning and filling the root canals, so the natural tooth can be saved instead of extracted.

Free consultation →

Masseter Botox (Jaw Botox)

Injections into the masseter muscle can ease teeth grinding (bruxism) and jaw tension and give the lower face a slimmer, more oval contour. A quick treatment whose effect typically lasts 4 to 6 months.

Free consultation →

TMJ Treatment

Treatment of pain, clicking or locking of the jaw joint, which is often linked to teeth grinding. Night guards (splints) protect the joint and relax the muscles; surgical options are available where needed.

Free consultation →

Orthodontics

Braces and clear aligners correct crooked, crowded or gapped teeth. Options for all ages include metal or tooth-coloured brackets and discreet clear aligner systems.

Free consultation →
